title: Planned Duration and the Deposit Basis of Professional Services Projects
content:
On a Professional Services Projects time-and-materials statement of work, the planned duration of the engagement sets the deposit basis to which the deposit percentage is applied.

## Clause

Where the planned duration of the engagement is the calendar days from the scheduled start date to the target completion date, an engagement planned to run 120 days or more has as its deposit basis its estimated fees multiplied by 90 and divided by its planned duration; an engagement planned to run fewer than 30 days has as its deposit basis the greater of its estimated fees and the class lowest original contract value; every other engagement has its estimated fees as its deposit basis.

| Planned duration in calendar days | Deposit basis |
|---|---|
| 120 or more | the estimated fees multiplied by 90, divided by the planned duration |
| 30 to 119 | the estimated fees |
| fewer than 30 | the greater of the estimated fees and the class lowest original contract value |

The class lowest original contract value for the classes that may be signed on time and materials:

| Quick Start Project | Standard Project | Advanced Project | Major Project | Strategic Program |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2500.00 | 10000.00 | 50000.00 | 150000.00 | 500000.00 |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

- Estimated fees 30000.00, planned duration 180 days: the deposit basis is 30000.00 multiplied by 90 and divided by 180, that is 15000.00.
- A Standard Project with estimated fees of 9500.00 planned to run 20 days: the deposit basis is the greater of 9500.00 and 10000.00, that is 10000.00.
- Planned durations of 30 and 119 days leave the estimated fees as the deposit basis; 120 days brings in the duration; 29 days brings in the class lowest value.
